analysis.title: GS Asia Macro: Global Market Recap - 2027 Outlooks
key_insights: USTs ended mixed Friday in a quiet session as a Microsoft outage reduced liquidity. The curve steepened (US 2s10s +4.5bps) as tech stocks fell and PPI rose less than expected. US 2-year yields fell about 3.5bps on the day but ended the week almost 35bps higher after hawkish Waller comments and firmer CPI raised rate-hike expectations.

Fed speakers on Friday were overwhelmingly hawkish and indicated the Fed has more work to do. This week brings more Fed speakers including Warsh on Monday, retail sales Tuesday and FOMC minutes Wednesday. Treasury supply includes $16bn 20-year bonds Wednesday and $19bn 10-year TIPS Thursday.
Trump is due to meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin on Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday.

Bunds sold off a further 3bps Friday and closed the week 13bps cheaper. Swaps price 72bps of ECB hikes by year-end 2027. BTPs tracked Bunds with the spread little changed, while OATs underperformed Bunds by 3bps.

Gilts bear steepened Friday. UK 10-year yields rose about 4bps to 5.34%, up 18bps on the week. BoE's Pill told the FT the BoE will probably need to raise rates further next year on top of a December increase, after last week's quarter-point hike to 4%.

JGBs: futures opened sharply lower after the rise in overseas yields and touched 82 sen lower before recovering. The curve closed bear steepening, and the report says the past few days' sell-off has erased the November rally. The desk expects upside in yields to stay heavy across the curve unless overseas yields turn lower, with auctions continuing.

Australian bonds bear steepened 3s10s by 1bp. The auction clearance rate fell to 44%, the lowest since April 2020, with 1,888 homes taken to auction, down 41.1% y/y (Cotality), as RBA hikes damp demand. The desk expects the October unemployment rate to stay at 4.7%.

US equities closed lower Friday, led by tech, amid uncertainty over the AI trade after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation. S&P -0.4%, Nasdaq -0.9%, Philly semiconductor index -3.4% (about -6% at its lows). Nvidia fell 2% and is down 13% on the week ahead of Tuesday earnings.
Retailers report this week: Home Depot Tuesday, Target and Lowe's Wednesday, Walmart and Gap Thursday.

GS Research 2027 outlook: global growth of 2.7% in 2026, forecast 2.8% in 2027 as lower energy prices and AI capex outweigh tighter financial conditions and more neutral fiscal policy. Risks are to the downside: renewed Iran escalation lifting energy prices, large fiscal deficits pushing long-term yields up (especially France), and AI capex disappointing.

GS expects two more Fed hikes and one ECB hike, with both returning to cuts in late 2027. Most of its other central bank forecasts are below market pricing, so it expects longer-term rates to fall modestly despite large deficits and heavy AI-linked borrowing.

GS markets outlook: bonds reclaim macro and hedging value (higher running yield, cheap valuations), further widening in US credit spreads is likely, equity index volatility has scope to rise, and the Dollar should soften through 2027 especially against JPY and CNY. European markets stay under pressure until the French election, keeping EUR downside attractive.

GS FX outlook: the Dollar may strengthen somewhat further against DM currencies in the near term before softening over 2027, with a reversal in commodity-sensitive currencies, continued AI spillovers in Asia and more durable policy support for the Yen.

market_movers.rationale: Nvidia fell 2% Friday and 13% on the week after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, ahead of earnings Tuesday.

sector_views.rationale: Tech led US equities lower Friday amid uncertainty over the AI trade. GS outlook says the AI investment impulse peaks and equity gains move from AI infrastructure to other areas, with risks if tighter financial conditions block the transition.

earnings_insights: Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday (Nov 17), after falling 13% on the week. No consensus figures are given.
Retailers reporting this week: Home Depot Tuesday, Target and Lowe's Wednesday, Walmart and Gap Thursday. No estimates are given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Contributed to the curve steepening on Friday, with the 2-year yield down about 3.5bps.
Up about 4bps Friday and 18bps on the week as the long end underperformed.
A quarter-point hike last week. BoE's Pill expects further increases, including one in December and more next year.
Market pricing in swaps after Bunds closed the week 13bps cheaper.
The desk expects the rate to remain stable in this week's labour force survey.
GS says growth was in line with potential.
GS forecast, supported by lower energy prices and AI capex.

risk_factors: Renewed Iran escalation could cause another energy price surge.
Large fiscal deficits could push long-term yields up more sharply, especially in France, and French election uncertainty may weigh on European markets.
AI capex could disappoint because of capacity constraints, regulation, credit market stress or weaker demand, and AI may be weighing on the job market.
Record credit and equity issuance requires discounted pricing in credit, with further US credit spread widening likely.
Hawkish Fed and BoE rhetoric and a global bond sell-off (Bunds, gilts, JGBs, USTs) are tightening financial conditions.
Uncertainty over Nvidia leadership after Jensen Huang's resignation.
vol_and_positioning: The Philly semiconductor index fell about 6% at its lows Friday and closed -3.4%.
GS says equity index volatility has scope to rise further, and recommends diversification from bonds and commodities as tail hedges.
The JGB desk note says shorts appear to have been covered to some extent, so investors' buying capacity has probably declined and the market looks vulnerable to selling pressure.
geopolitical: Iran targeted a Bahrain base but said the path to a US deal remains open (Bloomberg, Nov 15).
Trump is to meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit on Thursday.
The US and allies agreed to guard AI supply chains from China (FT).
GS lists renewed escalation in Iran causing an energy price surge as a downside risk to its 2027 outlook.
